mainTopic: Whether מגע and אהל combine, and the argument between אביי and רבא over when רבי יוסי calls an overhang 'touching'.
overview: The גמרא tests רבי יוחנן's idea that touching (מגע) and overhang (אהל) are one category, so that half a כזית of each adds up to make a person טמא. The סיפא of the משנה says they do not combine. רבי זירא answers that the רישא is a case of טומאה רצוצה, squeezed between two chests, where the overhang counts as touching. The גמרא then shows that רבי יוסי calls an overhang 'touching', from his ruling about a ladle of corpse dust. אביי and רבא disagree about what kind of overhang is called 'touching'. For אביי it means one less than a טפח above the טומאה. For רבא it means any overhang directly over the טומאה. רבא brings a proof from רבי יוסי's ruling about a net of bed bundles and window grilles spread over a corpse. אביי turns the proof aside by explaining that the net was never made part of the corpse like clothing, and that רבי יוסי holds hidden טומאה does not break through. The גמרא starts proving that last point from a משנה about a compartment in a chest, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the משנה: touching and overhang do not combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the סיפא of the משנה: if someone touches half a כזית, and some other object overhangs him and another half כזית, he stays טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who touches half an olive's worth of a dead body, while some other object covers both him and another half olive's worth, is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the end of the משנה as evidence. It is setting up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the person touches one half-כזית, and the other half-כזית reaches him only through a separate object overhanging both. The משנה says he is טהור, so the two halves did not add up. That looks like מגע and אהל are separate categories.

keyTerms.meaning: half an olive's size; half the minimum amount of a dead body that makes things טמא
overhangs or covers; spreads טומאה through a 'tent' (אהל)
some other object, not the person himself
pure; not made טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Here the person himself is not overhanging anything. A different object covers him and the half כזית, so the טומאה reaches him only through that object.

phrases.english: One who touches half an olive-bulk,
phrases.notes: This means flesh from a dead body. A full olive's size is needed to make someone טמא.

phrases.english: and another item overlies him
and over half an olive-bulk – he is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּכַחֲצִי זַיִת, וְדָבָר אַחֵר מַאֲהִיל עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of רבי יוחנן's view by bringing the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That מגע and אהל are separate categories that do not combine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה, which rules the person טהור.

steps.title: If they are one category, why is he pure?
steps.stepSummary: If מגע and אהל are one category, the סיפא should make him טמא. So the רישא, which seems to combine them, now becomes the problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if touching and overhang are one concept, why is he pure? So it is the first part of the משנה that is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that מגע and אהל are 'one name'. It says the beginning of the משנה is now the hard part to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If touching and overhang were truly one category, the two halves in the סיפא should add up to a full כזית, but the משנה says טהור. So the סיפא shows they are separate. That means the רישא, which seemed to combine them, needs a new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: one name; one legal category
why?
the first part of a משנה or ברייתא
it is difficult; an unresolved problem

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not reject the סיפא. It accepts the סיפא and says the רישא is what needs explaining.

phrases.english: But if it is one name,
phrases.notes: 'One name' means touching and overhanging count as one type of טומאה.

phrases.english: why is he pure?
Rather, the first clause is difficult.
phrases.notes: The first clause said touching half and overhanging half makes him טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי חַד שְׁמָא הוּא, אַמַּאי טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the סיפא from step 1 to raise a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that מגע and אהל are one category, and the plain reading of the רישא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא shows they do not combine, so the רישא cannot be read as combining real מגע with real אהל.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the רישא is about טומאה pressed between two chests
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains the רישא as a case of טומאה רצוצה, טומאה squeezed between two chests with less than a טפח of space. There the overhang counts as touching, so the whole case is really touching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: We are dealing with טומאה squeezed between two chests with no opening of a handbreadth between them, so it is all touching.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the difficulty by giving the רישא a special case. In that case both halves reach the person by touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When טומאה is squeezed into a space smaller than a טפח, it 'bursts upward' and is treated like it touches whatever is above it. So the 'overhang' in the רישא is really a kind of touching. Both halves join because both are מגע, not because מגע and אהל combine.

keyTerms.meaning: compressed טומאה, squeezed into a space with no open handbreadth
chests or cabinets
an open space of one handbreadth, needed to form a real אהל
touching

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer removes the proof that מגע and אהל are one category, so the רישא no longer supports רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּטוּמְאָה רְצוּצָה בֵּין שְׁנֵי מִגְדָּלִים עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: We are dealing with impurity pressed between two chests,
and there is no opening of a handbreadth between them,
so all of it is touching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: בְּטוּמְאָה רְצוּצָה בֵּין שְׁנֵי מִגְדָּלִים עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא on the רישא from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a special situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא seemed to join real touching with real overhang.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is about טומאה רצוצה, where the overhang counts as touching, so both halves are מגע.

steps.title: Which תנא calls overhang 'touching'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא would use the word 'touching' for this kind of overhang.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who calls an overhang 'touching'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who would describe an overhang with the word 'touching'. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא returns to רבי יוחנן's reading of the thigh-bone משנה on 125a: its word 'touching' covers an overhang. It now asks which תנא uses 'touching' this way.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage of the משנה period
calls; names
tent; overhang that spreads טומאה

phrases.english: And who is the tanna
who calls a tent 'touches'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוחנן's reading on 125a, after רבי זירא set aside the proof from the half-measure משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא uses the word 'touching' for an overhang.

steps.title: It is רבי יוסי: a ladle of רקב makes טמא by touching, carrying and overhang
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא is רבי יוסי. It quotes his ברייתא that a full ladle of corpse dust (רקב) makes things טמא by מגע, משא and אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יוסי, as it is taught: רבי יוסי says: A full ladle of corpse dust makes things טמא by touching, by carrying, and by overhang.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי יוסי as the תנא and brings his ברייתא as the source. The proof from this ברייתא is still being set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי rules that a ladle of רקב spreads טומאה through touching. The ברייתא is brought to show that רבי יוסי uses 'touching' for this kind of case. The full explanation of how it proves this comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: a full ladle of decayed corpse dust
contact; spreading טומאה by touching
carrying; spreading טומאה by lifting
makes טמא

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yosei,
as it is taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
A full ladle of dust
phrases.notes: This means dust from a decayed dead body.

phrases.english: imparts impurity by contact, and by carrying, and in a tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא is רבי יוסי, shown from his ברייתא about a ladle of רקב.

steps.title: In רבי יוסי's ברייתא, 'touching' must mean overhanging
steps.stepSummary: Carrying or overhanging a ladle of רקב covers all of it, but a hand cannot touch all the loose dust. So 'נוגע' in the ברייתא must mean overhanging.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that carrying and overhanging work, because a person carries all the dust and overhangs all the dust. But touching? He does not touch all of it! So this must prove that 'touching' here means overhanging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the ברייתא of רבי יוסי from step 5 proves he uses the word 'touching' for an overhang.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full ladle of רקב is the minimum amount needed to make things טמא. When you carry it or overhang it, you deal with the whole amount. Your hand touches only part of the loose dust, so 'touching' can only work if it means overhanging.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (this part is fine, but...)
Carries
Learn from it: a proof is being drawn

phrases.english: It makes sense with carrying and with a tent,
since this one carries all of it,
and that one overhangs all of it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נוֹגֵעַ – הָא לָא נָגַע בְּכוּלֵּיהּ!
phrases.english: But touching? He does not touch all of it!
So isn't it right to learn from this:
what does 'touching' mean? Overhanging.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא quoted in step 5 proves that רבי יוסי calls an overhang 'touching'.
steps.raayaObject: That a תנא, רבי יוסי, uses the word 'נוגע' for an overhang
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's ברייתא: a full ladle of רקב makes things טמא by מגע, משא and אהל

steps.title: The same ברייתא lists touching and overhanging separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבי יוסי lists 'touching' and 'overhanging' as two separate items, so how can one of them mean the other?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he teaches 'touching', and he also teaches 'overhanging'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from step 6. If touching just means overhanging, why does the ברייתא list both?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Listing two things side by side suggests they are different. If 'נוגע' means overhanging, the list seems to say the same thing twice. The step 6 reading now looks forced.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching, one way of becoming טמא
Overhanging, forming an אהל over the טומאה
A 'tent': something that covers both a person and טומאה, or that covers the טומאה

phrases.english: But it teaches 'touching',
and it also teaches 'overhanging'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'נוגע' in רבי יוסי's ברייתא means overhanging
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists 'נוגע' and 'מאהיל' as separate items, so they cannot be the same thing.

steps.title: אביי: a low overhang is 'touching', a high one is plain tent
steps.stepSummary: אביי says there are two kinds of overhang. Less than a טפח above the טומאה is called a 'touching' tent; more than a טפח is just a tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: below a טפח, it is a 'touching' tent. Above a טפח, it is just a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by splitting overhanging into two kinds, so the ברייתא is listing two different things after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, 'נוגע' means an overhang within a טפח of the dust, which is close enough to count as touching. 'מאהיל' means a higher overhang, which is a regular אהל. So the list does not repeat itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, the key height in the laws of אהל
Less than a טפח high
A 'touching' tent: an overhang treated like touching
Merely, just plain

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְמַטָּה מִטֶּפַח – אֹהֶל נְגִיעָה,
phrases.english: Abaye said: below a handbreadth, it is a 'touching' tent;
above a handbreadth, it is merely a tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two kinds of overhang based on height
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'touching' means overhanging, the ברייתא seemed to list the same thing twice.
steps.terutzMaskana: An overhang within a טפח is 'touching'; one above a טפח is plain אהל, so the list names two different cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects to רבי זירא's טומאה רצוצה in step 3, where the low, squeezed space is what makes the overhang count as touching.

steps.title: רבא: even a high overhang is 'touching'; plain tent means spreading
steps.stepSummary: רבא says any overhang directly over the טומאה, even above a טפח, is a 'touching' tent. Plain אהל means a roof that spreads the טומאה to a person who is under it but not over the טומאה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: even above a טפח it is also a 'touching' tent. So what is plain tent? Spreading.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the challenge of step 7, drawing the line in a different place than אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, height does not matter. Being directly over the טומאה is always 'touching'. 'מאהיל' in the ברייתא is a different case: a roof over both the טומאה and the person, which carries the טומאה to him.

keyTerms.meaning: More than a טפח high
What is the case? How does it look?
Spreading: a roof carrying טומאה from its source to someone else under it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two answers. For אביי, height decides between 'touching' and plain tent. For רבא, it depends on whether you are over the טומאה itself or only under the same roof.

phrases.english: Rava said: even above a handbreadth,
it is also a 'touching' tent.
So what is the case of merely a tent?
With spreading.
phrases.notes: He means a roof that covers both the טומאה and the person, bringing the טומאה over to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַעְלָה מִטֶּפַח נָמֵי אֹהֶל נְגִיעָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the קשיא of step 7, disagreeing with אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different definition of 'touching' tent versus plain tent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי held that height decides between a 'touching' tent and a plain tent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any overhang directly over the טומאה is 'touching'; plain אהל is a roof that spreads the טומאה to someone else.

steps.title: רבא brings a source from רבי יוסי about bed bundles and window grilles
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports his view with another ruling of רבי יוסי: bed bundles and window grilles between a house and its upper floor act as a barrier, so טומאה does not pass to the other side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? As we learned: רבי יוסי says, bundles of a bed and window grilles form a barrier between the house and the upper floor, so that the טומאה does not go into the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts proving his opinion by quoting another ruling of רבי יוסי. This step sets up the proof; how it proves his point comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא about רקב is also from רבי יוסי, רבא looks at how רבי יוסי deals with אהל elsewhere. Here רבי יוסי says these items block טומאה between the two floors. רבא will use this ruling to show how רבי יוסי thinks about plain אהל.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (Introducing a source for one's opinion)
Bundles of a bed (bundled reeds or ropes)
Lattices or grilles of windows
Form a barrier, block the טומאה
Upper floor or attic

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it?
As we learned: Rabbi Yosei says:
bundles of a bed and grilles of windows
phrases.notes: These are laid as a ceiling between the lower room and the upper room.

phrases.english: form a barrier between the house and the upper floor,
so that טומאה does not come into the other side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא brings a source for the view he stated in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that plain אהל means spreading (המשכה), and that any overhang directly over the טומאה is 'touching'
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's ruling that bed bundles and window grilles block טומאה between a house and its upper floor

steps.title: The bundles and grilles spread like a net over a corpse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if the bundles and grilles are spread over a corpse in the open air, someone 'touching' over a hole becomes טמא, and someone over the solid part stays טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one spread them over the corpse in the open air, a person who 'touches' opposite the hole is טמא, and one not opposite the hole is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי יוסי's ברייתא from the previous step. This last clause is the part רבא will use as his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the bundles and grilles are not between two floors. They are hanging over a corpse like a net. The טומאה rises through the holes but is blocked by the solid parts. The key detail is that the ברייתא uses the word 'נוגע' for someone above the net.

keyTerms.meaning: He spread them out (like a net)
In the open air, hanging above
A hole (in the netting)
Impure / pure

phrases.english: If one spread them over the corpse in the air,
one who 'touches' opposite the hole is impure,
phrases.notes: 'Touches' here means being right above the corpse, not physically touching it.

phrases.english: one not opposite the hole is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that a covering above a טפח directly over the טומאה is still called 'touching'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The netting clause of רבי יוסי's ברייתא

steps.title: The net cannot be less than a טפח above the corpse
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what height the net is at. If it were less than a טפח above, it would count as the corpse's clothing, and someone over the solid part should be טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say the net was less than a טפח above, why is someone not over the hole טהור? It is like a corpse wearing its clothing, and a corpse in its clothing makes things טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to explain his proof. He first shows that the net cannot be less than a טפח above the corpse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothing on a corpse does not block its טומאה, so a person over a clothed corpse is טמא. A net that close to the corpse should count the same way. Then the solid parts should not protect anyone, but the ברייתא says they do. So the case cannot be below a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances?
If you say
A handbreadth
A corpse in its clothing, which does not block its טומאה

phrases.english: What is the case?
If we say it was below a handbreadth,
then one not opposite the hole, why is he pure?
It is a corpse in its clothing,
phrases.notes: A net this close to the body is treated like the dead person's clothes.

phrases.english: and a corpse in its clothing imparts impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא from step 11 by ruling out the below-a-טפח reading.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that a covering more than a טפח above the טומאה is still called 'נוגע' (eliminating the below-a-טפח reading)
steps.raayaSupportSource: Below a טפח the net would count as the corpse's clothing (מת בכסותו), which does not block טומאה. That contradicts the ברייתא's ruling that one not opposite the hole is טהור.

steps.title: So a covering above a טפח is still called 'touching'
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that the net must be more than a טפח above. Even so, the ברייתא calls it 'נוגע', which supports his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be above a טפח, and still he calls it 'touching'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא completes his proof. The net is above a טפח, yet רבי יוסי calls it 'touching'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said only a covering less than a טפח above the טומאה is called a 'touching' tent. This ברייתא calls a covering above a טפח 'נוגע'. That matches רבא: anything directly over the טומאה is a 'touching' tent, at any height.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (introduces the only remaining option)
More than a handbreadth above
He calls it

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof: the net must be over a טפח high (or it would be like clothing), and the ברייתא still calls it 'נוגע'.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not above a handbreadth,
and he calls it 'touching'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion once step 12 rules out the below-a-טפח reading.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's definition of a 'touching' tent (step 9) against אביי's (step 8)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's use of 'נוגע' for a net more than a טפח above the corpse

steps.title: אביי: the net is not like clothing because it was never made part of the corpse
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the net really is less than a טפח above. Clothing counts as part of the corpse because it is treated as part of the body, but this net is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, it is below a טפח. As for what you said, that it is like a corpse in its clothing: with clothing, the person makes it part of the corpse. This net, he does not make part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבא's proof. He keeps the case below a טפח and explains why the net still blocks טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothing fails to block טומאה only because it becomes part of the corpse (בטול). A net spread temporarily over the body is never treated that way, so it stays a separate covering and blocks the טומאה. So the case can be below a טפח, which fits אביי's view that only coverings under a טפח are called 'touching'.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (keeps the original reading)
He makes it part of something else, so it loses its separate status

steps.confusionAlert: Being less than a טפח away does not by itself make something 'clothing'. What matters is whether it was made part of the corpse.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי: clothing does not block a corpse's טומאה only because it was made part of the corpse. A temporary net was not, so it blocks even when less than a טפח away.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Actually, it is below a handbreadth,
and as for what you said, 'it is a corpse in its clothing':
with a corpse in its clothing, he makes it part of it,
this one, he does not make it part of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof in steps 12-13 by undoing the assumption that a net below a טפח counts as clothing.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The step that ruled out the below-a-טפח reading (step 12)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed anything within a טפח counts as clothing. Clothing only fails to block because it was made part of the corpse, and the net was not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the rule that clothing fails to block a corpse's טומאה because it is treated as part of the body, not because of how close it is.

steps.title: Shouldn't the net count as covered impurity that breaks upward?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: a covering less than a טפח above a corpse should make it טומאה טמונה, which breaks through and rises up.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it be like hidden impurity, which breaks through and rises up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer from step 14. Even if the net is not the corpse's clothing, it is still something covering the corpse very closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that when טומאה is covered with less than a טפח of space, it 'breaks through' upward. That would make even the solid part of the net pass on טומאה. So someone over the solid part should be טמא, but the ברייתא said he is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Hidden or covered impurity: a source of טומאה with less than a טפח of space around it
Breaks through and rises up: the טומאה goes straight up through the covering

phrases.english: But let it be like hidden impurity
which breaks through and rises up?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's rejection in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the net is less than a טפח above the corpse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Less than a טפח of cover makes it טומאה טמונה, which breaks upward. Then the solid part should also pass on טומאה, which contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי holds hidden impurity does not break through
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבי יוסי, the author of the ברייתא, holds that טומאה טמונה does not break through.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds that hidden impurity does not break through.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי. The rule of 'breaking through' is not accepted by רבי יוסי, and the ברייתא follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed everyone agrees that covered טומאה breaks upward. The answer is that רבי יוסי disagrees. So, in his view, only someone over a hole becomes טמא, just as the ברייתא said.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds: introduces the opinion a sage follows
Does not break through

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds:
Hidden impurity does not break through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: The author of the source holds a different rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Covered טומאה always breaks upward, so the solid part of the net should pass on טומאה
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי holds טומאה טמונה does not break through, so אביי's reading stands

steps.title: Source: the compartment in a chest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof of רבי יוסי's view and brings a משנה: in a compartment with a narrow opening, טומאה inside makes the house טמא, but טומאה in the house does not enter the compartment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say this? As we learned in a משנה: a compartment of a chest that has an inner space of a טפח, but its opening is less than a טפח. If טומאה is inside it, the house is טמא. If טומאה is in the house, what is inside the compartment is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know רבי יוסי holds this, and starts quoting a משנה. This first part is the view of the תנא קמא; רבי יוסי's view comes in step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The compartment has room inside, but its opening is narrower than a טפח. According to the תנא קמא, טומאה from inside still goes out into the house, but טומאה from the house does not go in. This sets up the contrast with רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this?: asks for a source
A compartment in a chest or cabinet
An open space of one טפח, the minimum size for an אהל
Its opening, the way out of the compartment

phrases.english: And from where do you say this? As we learned:
A compartment of a chest
that has an open space of a handbreadth
but its opening does not have a handbreadth,
if impurity is inside it, the house is impure;
if impurity is in the house, what is inside it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Seeks a source for the claim in step 16
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי holds טומאה טמונה does not break through
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in אהלות about a compartment in a chest

steps.title: Why impurity goes out but not in
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the תנא קמא: טומאה normally goes out of a place, but does not normally come in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the way of טומאה is to go out, and the way of טומאה is not to come in.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason for the תנא קמא's split ruling. This is still part of the setup before רבי יוסי argues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source of טומאה inside the compartment will eventually be taken out, and it will pass through the opening. So the house is already treated as טמא. But nothing forces טומאה from the house to come into the compartment.

keyTerms.meaning: The way of טומאה is to go out: it will eventually be removed through the opening
To enter

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this with רבי יוסי's view. This reason belongs to the תנא קמא; רבי יוסי disagrees in the next line.

phrases.english: because the way of impurity is to go out,
and the way of impurity is not to come in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the תנא קמא's ruling in step 17

steps.title: רבי יוסי rules the house pure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules the house טהור, because the טומאה might be removed in small pieces or burned where it lies. The proof about covered טומאה is not drawn from this line but from the סיפא quoted in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי rules it pure, because one can take it out in halves, or burn it in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי יוסי's dissent: he rules the house טהור even when the טומאה is inside the compartment. The גמרא then goes on to quote the סיפא (next step), which is what its proof is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says the טומאה won't necessarily leave through the opening as a full-sized piece. It could be cut into pieces too small to pass on טומאה, or burned inside the compartment. His reason is about whether the טומאה will come out, not about breaking through. The proof for step 16 is drawn from the סיפא quoted in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules it pure
In halves: in pieces each smaller than the amount that passes on טומאה
To burn it in its place

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei rules it pure,
phrases.notes: He is talking about the house, when the טומאה is inside the compartment.

phrases.english: because one can take it out in halves,
or burn it in its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוסי's dissent in the משנה, part of the source being built to prove step 16
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי holds טומאה טמונה does not break through
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's ruling in the משנה of the chest compartment

steps.title: The compartment in the doorway with its opening facing outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the סיפא of the משנה. If the compartment stands in the doorway with its opening facing outside, טומאה inside it leaves the house טהור, and טומאה in the house leaves what is inside the compartment טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the last part of that משנה teaches: If someone placed the compartment in the doorway, with its opening facing outside, then if there is טומאה inside it, the house stays טהור. If there is טומאה in the house, whatever is inside the compartment stays טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps building its proof by quoting the last part of the same משנה. It describes a new setup: the compartment stands in the doorway with its opening facing outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the compartment's opening faced into the house, so טומאה inside it was expected to come out into the house. Now the opening faces outside, so the טומאה would leave toward the outside and not through the house. The house stays טהור even though the טומאה sits covered inside the compartment. The גמרא uses this to show that covered טומאה does not break up into the house, and that inference continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part (end clause) of a משנה or ברייתא
He placed it (the compartment) in the doorway of the house
Its opening faces outside, away from the house
A source of טומאה is inside the compartment

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the first case. There the compartment's opening led into the house, so טומאה inside it made the house טמא. Here the opening faces outside, so the house stays טהור.

phrases.english: And the latter clause teaches:
If he placed it in the entrance, and its opening faces outside,
if there is impurity inside it, the house is pure;
if there is impurity in the house, whatever is inside it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same משנה used to prove רבי יוסי's view, adding its final clause.
steps.raayaObject: That covered טומאה (טומאה טמונה) does not break through and spread into the house.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה about the compartment: when it stands in the doorway with its opening facing outside, טומאה inside leaves the house טהור.
